protocol: 12 h horizon, both streams, features = forecast.FEATURES, test days 2026-09-28..2026-10-17 (20 days, all exam days inside). To bound runtime every model is retrained every 5 days, at midnight 09-28, 10-03, 10-08 and 10-13, on features(hourly(as_of=d)) with targets before d, and each fit serves the next 5 days; the same schedule applies to every model. All models are scored on the same rows (rows where any prediction is NaN are dropped). Non-GB models: NaN filled with the training median per column; Ridge and MLP use one-hot building/day_type and standard scaling, RandomForest the imputed ordinal features. Ridge(alpha=1); RandomForest(100 trees, min_samples_leaf=5, 1 job); MLP (64,32), early_stopping, max_iter=300; our model = forecast.fit. LSTM: single layer, hidden 32, input = last 168 hourly values of the building ending 12 h before the target (scaled per building with training mean/std, NaN -> 0) concatenated with the target hour's calendar features (hour/dow sin-cos, day_type one-hot, building one-hot, is_event, scaled temp), linear head, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 256, 5 epochs, MSE, one CPU thread, seed 0. Metrics: MAE, WAPE = 100*sum|err|/sum(actual) overall, on exam days and on working days. size_kb = joblib compress=3 (state_dict for the LSTM), train_s = mean seconds per fit, predict_ms = median wall time to prepare inputs and predict one building's 12 rows, one thread. Other processes were running on this machine, so timings are noisy (see load).
